truths.truth: The 10 ms p99 hook budget holds over 100 runs of every event against a store built from the real corpus
truths.evidence: crates/verbatim/tests/corpus.rs:422 asserts a profile-aware wall - `if cfg!(debug_assertions) { ("debug", 20.0) } else { ("release", 10.0) }` - and the assert at :493 compares p99 against that budget. `cargo test` builds debug by default, so the number actually enforced by a normal run is 20 ms, not the flat 10 ms AC4 and this item state. SUMMARY.md:71-76 records the debug measurement at p50 18.48 ms / p99 19.72 ms against that 20.0 ms wall (1.4% margin) and rising with corpus growth; release measured p99 4.26 ms. Not re-run here: the arm is gated on VERBATIM_TEST_CORPUS and a corpus ingest costs ~355 s

gaps.name: The 10 ms p99 cold-start budget over the real corpus
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the criterion as written is not what the code asserts. corpus.rs asserts 10 ms only in release; in the debug profile `cargo test` builds by default it asserts 20 ms, and the recorded debug measurement is 19.72 ms p99 against that wall (1.4% margin), on a number that grows with the corpus
gaps.evidence: crates/verbatim/tests/corpus.rs:422 `let (profile, budget) = if cfg!(debug_assertions) { ("debug", 20.0_f64) } else { ("release", 10.0_f64) };` and the assertion at corpus.rs:493-496. SUMMARY.md deviation 2 and 3 and the first open item record the 18.48/19.72 ms debug figures and attribute the cost to v0.1.0's INJ-01 index pointer at crates/verbatim-core/src/inject/brief.rs:580, not to this phase's AND (debug p50 10.24 ms with the AND reverted vs 10.38 ms with it)
gaps.missing: Adjudicate AC4: either reword it to the shipped profile-aware wall (10 ms release, headroom-only debug arm), or fix the INJ-01 index pointer count so a single 10 ms wall holds in both profiles. Whichever way it goes, the 20 ms debug wall has 1.4% margin against a measurement that climbs every time this project is worked on, so leaving it as an asserting wall queues a failure that is not a regression
